# Statement-coverage baseline for the merged unit + acceptance profile.
#
# `scripts/coverage-readme.sh` renders README.md's badge and coverage block from
# this file, and `scripts/coverage-gate.sh` fails a run whose merged coverage
# falls below a `floor_*` value. The badge, the block and the gate therefore
# cannot disagree: they all read this file, and CI fails when README.md is out
# of sync with it.
#
# Keys. `measured_<scope>` names a scope and needs a matching `floor_<scope>`;
# `_` is the path separator in the rendered label, so `measured_internal_client`
# renders `internal/client`. `measured_total` is required and drives the badge.
# `measured_commit` and `measured_date` describe the last measurement,
# `target`/`gold` are the tracked milestones.
#
# The gate is `make coverage-gate` (`scripts/coverage-gate.sh`), which the
# `Coverage` job runs on every pull request after the acceptance container has
# written its profile. It parses this file with the same rules as
# `coverage-readme.sh` and additionally requires every scope named here to appear
# in the merged profile: a missing, misspelled or stray `floor_*`, or a scope
# that drops out of the profile, is a configuration error (exit 2), never a pass.
#
# The measurement is the merged profile the committed tooling produces: the bare
# unit profile (`make coverage`, `coverage.out`) merged with the instrumented
# acceptance container's profile (`coverage-acceptance.out`,
# `-covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./internal/...`) by `scripts/merge-coverage.sh`
# (`make coverage-merge`). To raise the floor: run `make coverage` and
# `make coverage-merge`, update `measured_*` and `floor_*` here, then run
# `make coverage-readme` and commit the result.
#
# `measured_*` is what the project last observed; `floor_*` is the enforced
# minimum, kept half a point below the measurement (rounded down to the next half
# point) so environment jitter cannot fail a run on its own.
#
# The scopes below the four original ones are the areas the coverage issues named
# as real gaps; each floor is only as high as the tests committed with it. A floor
# is never lowered: raising one is a deliberate line in a pull request.
#
# Deliberately not a scope: internal/datasources/secrets. It wraps the Gravitino
# 1.4 secrets API, which cannot be exercised against the 1.3.0/1.3.1 servers this
# provider supports, so a floor there would measure the fake only.

# Last measurement: merged unit + acceptance on Go 1.27.2, 7,661 statements.
measured_internal_client=79.7
measured_internal_models=86.3
measured_internal_provider=94.6
measured_internal_client_auth=76.7
measured_internal_datasources_schema=94.6
measured_internal_datasources_policy=86.1
measured_internal_datasources_role=85.6
measured_internal_datasources_fileset=86.5
measured_internal_datasources_partition=92.2
measured_internal_resources_partition=92.4
measured_total=83.4
measured_commit=c2fc783
measured_date=2026-10-19

# Enforced floor.
floor_internal_client=79.0
floor_internal_models=85.5
floor_internal_provider=94.0
floor_internal_client_auth=76.0
floor_internal_datasources_schema=94.0
floor_internal_datasources_policy=85.5
floor_internal_datasources_role=85.0
floor_internal_datasources_fileset=86.0
floor_internal_datasources_partition=91.5
floor_internal_resources_partition=91.5
floor_total=82.5

# Milestones tracked in the issue tracker.
target=80
gold=90
